owner: akiendelllinux_cc_0 (CC) gates writes. The shape is Akien's design, 2026-07-26, verbatim sketch preserved below.
intention: Attach dependencies to the WORKFLOW STAGE that needs them, not to the ticket as a whole — and make the act of LOOKING compile back into the ticket. A stage declares what it needs; whenever anyone checks the world, the finding is stamped onto that need with WHAT, WHEN and HOW MEASURED. Retire the ad-hoc `waits_on` field once its content is migrated.
why: Two failures measured on 2026-07-26, and they have one fix. FIRST: dependency had no honest representation. `waits_on` is authored by hand on 6 of 10 staged tickets, is in NO node-class schema, is PROSE (voyage.py:75 already says so: 'the ticket's prose waits_on is narrative, not a clean party to render'), is consumed by nothing, and is DROPPED at berthing — zero of 25 berthed charters carry it. So the dependency record is destroyed by the act of finishing. SECOND: the record kept disagreeing with the world — 'awaiting Akien's signature' when there was nowhere to sign; 'no inference host' with ollama serving on :11434 for four days. Akien's shape fixes both: needs are declared per-stage (intrinsic, stable), and the OBSERVATION is compiled in even when nobody picks the ticket up — so going and looking is what keeps the record honest, and the two can no longer drift.
akiens_sketch_verbatim: 'the workflow is the stages, but dependencies can be outside influences. so we can't represent dependencies directly by just saying workflow. each workflow step should list it's dependenices. so BUILD might be gated on BUS DEVICE and EMBEDDINGS GENERATOR... and just be listed like: [ ] BUILD - Needs: - BUS DEVICE - EMBEDDINGS GENERATOR etc. then whenever we look at the state of the things, if there's an update we mark it: [ ] BUILD - Needs: [DONE] BUS DEVICE - EMBEDDINGS GENERATOR — even if we don't pick up the ticket! the fact that we went and looked gets compiled into the ticket.'
traces_to: Law 1 — 'the fact that we went and looked gets compiled into the ticket' IS Law 1: the answered question becomes structure, so the next mind reads the measurement instead of repeating it.
Law 3 — a need's status is a MEASUREMENT with a time and a method, not an assertion. A bare [DONE] is an unmeasured claim wearing a checkmark.
Law 4 — the shape is enforced by the schema and the write door, not by anyone remembering to update prose.
Law 7 — a stale mark must be VISIBLE as stale; collapsing 'measured three weeks ago' into 'done' is a record of truth losing information.

falsifier: A mark lacking WHEN or HOW MEASURED must be REFUSED at the write door — a bare [DONE] cannot be written. Staleness must be QUERYABLE: given a ticket, the system reports the age of each mark, so 'this DONE is 21 days old' is a fact on the surface rather than an invisible assumption. And the shape must carry a REAL case end-to-end: the librarian's BUILD stage needs {inference host, embeddings generator, store design}; the host mark must record today's measurement (ollama :11434, three models, embed 768d, 2026-07-26) and the other two must sit unmarked. A hollow build — a checkbox with no timestamp, or a needs list nothing can query — fails every clause.
horizon: Re-read when the FIRST ticket is picked up under this shape. The open question the gate surfaced: does a mark ever EXPIRE by itself (a host can go down after being marked DONE), or is age always reported and judged by the reader? Deliberately NOT guessed — no expiry has been measured as needed, and inventing a TTL ahead of evidence is the same error as guessing a chatter-damping width. Filed, not built.
distinctions_recorded: PER-STAGE, NOT PER-TICKET — and this is what makes it storable at all. CC argued against a stored `waits_on` on the grounds that ordering is GOAL-RELATIVE (the same ticket sits differently depending on whether we aim at the librarian or elsewhere), so a stored edge freezes one target's answer. That objection is real and it does NOT apply here: 'BUILD needs the bus device' is intrinsic to that stage, true regardless of the goal. The goal-relative part — the ORDER — is still derived at ask time; only the intrinsic need is stored.

THE MARK IS AN OBSERVATION, NOT A CHECKBOX. {status, when, how measured} — the same three fields a VALIDATION carries, and the same reason a host-seam carries a re-runnable verify and a seal that expires. This shape surfaced TWICE in one session from unrelated directions (here, and as the staleness marker a cached embedding needs), which is evidence it is a primitive in this system rather than a local convenience.

IT RIDES THE STATE/HISTORY SPLIT THAT ALREADY EXISTS. An observation is append-only truth (history); the current mark is a compiled view (state). So this needs no new storage mechanism — it needs the projector's append door, which as of 2026-07-25 also has a shape gate to refuse a malformed mark. The per-component schema declaration filed on that door is exactly the edge this node pulls.

DIVERGENCE FROM THIS TICKET'S OWN FILED DISTINCTION, ARGUED NOT ASSUMED. The cast said marks ride the projector's append door. They do not, and cannot yet: that door writes a COMPONENT's history.json/state.json pair and a staged ticket has neither — a ticket's voyage freezes into history when it PROVES OUT (CLAUDE.md), so routing marks there would mint a history file per staged ticket and invert that design. The mark lands in the ticket record through one function (needs.mark), reusing the projector's discipline (validate-before-write, append-only, atomic write) rather than its file pair. AND IT DELIVERS THE WHY BETTER: because the mark rides INSIDE the ticket, it MIGRATES when the ticket berths beside its code — which is precisely the 'dependency record destroyed by finishing the work' failure this node exists to fix.

`MISSING` IS CC'S COINAGE AND IS FLAGGED FOR RATIFY. Akien's sketch has [DONE] and unmarked; it has no word for 'we went and looked and the thing is NOT there'. That case is the whole point of 'even if we don't pick up the ticket', so it needs a status. DONE is his word, kept. MISSING is mine — derivable in the native domain (a dependency that is not there is missing), but mine until he rules. Owed a ratify-or-reject, like `crossing`.

BUILDING THE CONSUMER IS WHAT TESTED THE CLAIM. needs.py binds to a node's stage vocabulary, which meant parsing 17 live workflow strings for the first time — and only 6 could be parsed at all, with a 7th parsing to FICTION (see the trouble). The chokepoint's own proof said 'the state vocabulary is physics, not /sorted's prose'; it was prose on 11 of 17 nodes. The generalisation worth keeping: a claim that something is physics is only tested when a SECOND reader depends on it, because the first reader can be wrong in the same direction as the writer.
children: a — THE SHAPE: BUILT + PROVEN + SEALED 2026-07-26 (cairn/base/needs.py). Per-stage needs validated against the node's OWN parsed stage vocabulary, so a need cannot attach to a stage the node does not have. The observation mark is {status, when, how_measured} and the door REFUSES a bare [DONE], a token how_measured ('checked'), an unageable when ('yesterday'), and a status invented for 'never looked' — that third condition is the ABSENCE of a mark, never a writable status. Marks are append-only with monotonic seq; the current view is a pure projection carrying AGE IN DAYS from an INJECTED today, so staleness is queryable and the proof cannot go stale. Akien's sketch is RENDERED (render_needs) because his shape is the spec of the surface, and unmeasured() names the category every one of 2026-07-26's stumbles lived in. 13 teeth; hollow-build checked by gutting the gate and watching it red.

b — THE STALENESS QUERY, SHIPPED AS `cairn whatsnext`: given a ticket (or all tickets), report each mark's age and method, so 'what's next?' reads measurements rather than assertions. IT IS A COMMAND, NOT A SKILL — Akien's reason, 2026-07-26: 'that you and i can both read'. One implementation, two readers; a /whatsnext skill would be a second implementation of the same logic for CC only, so any skill that needs it CALLS the command. bin/cairn is a dumb dispatcher and its own header says 'New verbs are just a new executable in bin/cmd/ — no edit here', so this adds a file and changes nothing else. THE VIEW IS DERIVED ON READ, never a maintained file: a file that persists between reads is a cache that drifts, which recreates the record-vs-world defect this whole node exists to close (the pattern is intentions_model_compiler's — compile-if-stale on read, the read IS the event, no daemon). It may WRITE an output file for human reading, regenerated and never hand-edited, same rule as `state`. Waits on a.

filed_edges: THE DEPENDENCY TREE IS A VIEW IN harbor_master, NOT A NEW DEVICE. Akien asked whether it wants its own device (a 'dependency map maintainer') or belongs to harbor_master. It belongs there, per Law 6: harbor_master/register.py already compiles the fleet register from the SAME source (berthed charters plus open tickets), so a second device over it would mint a second owner of one truth. Akien's own framing is the reason to keep them together — the register is PRESENT tense, the dependency tree is NEAR-FUTURE tense, one owner, two tenses. And there is nothing to MAINTAIN: the view is derived, so a maintainer would be a poll with a job title. Composing the three inputs (where each boat is · what its next stage needs · when we last looked and how) yields the three answers that matter: what can move now, what is blocked on a MEASUREMENT NOBODY HAS TAKEN, and what is blocked on real work. That middle category is where every one of 2026-07-26's stumbles lived, and it has been invisible until now.

Ticket-writing since then has co-opted the same key for CHART stages. Measured split of the 13 tickets carrying it: FOUR workflow-keyed (inference-host-wiring, intention-extractor, orient-prebuild, post-build-inspector — all ['BUILDME']) and NINE chart-keyed (a-node-holds-one-claim, a-pane-declares-its-view, a-voyage-names-its-ticket, nothing-rides-loose, proved-answers-the-chart, sail-pins-its-refusals, skills-ride-the-chokepoint, the-deposit-rides-the-read, watchme-emits-a-probe — keyed orient/constrain/survey/decompose/triage/hypothesize/validate). The proof reds on the first chart-keyed ticket it reaches: "stage 'orient' is not in this node's workflow vocabulary ['THINKME','TICKETME','BUILDME','PROVEME','LEARNME','PROVED'] — a need cannot attach to a stage the node does not have".

(z2) THE GATE IS RIGHT AND THE DATA IS WRONG, WHICH IS WHY IT IS NOT A BUG IN needs.py. The vocabulary check is this ticket's own physics doing its job — it caught a real conflation. Both usages are legitimate: a workflow stage and a chart stage are different axes (WHERE the node stands vs WHICH preamble brick), and a need genuinely attaches to both. My read, UNRATIFIED: give the chart usage its own key (`chart_needs`), leaving `stage_needs` meaning exactly what this ticket minted it to mean, and migrate the nine. The alternative — widening needs.py's vocabulary to accept chart stages — makes one key mean two things and puts the drift back where it cannot be seen. NOT TAKEN: which key wins is a naming/vocabulary decision and this ticket owns it; renaming a field on nine live tickets from inside another voyage would be exactly the silent widening /sail forbids. Wants Akien's signature gate. Until then the red stands, loud, and is reported as a known red rather than fixed in passing.
